titles: the storage engine is an embedded SQLite database reached through a version-pinned, gate-observable binding
the database handle is owned by a dedicated worker thread and never escapes it
a transaction handle is an opaque token that cannot be used to reach the database
the connection factory opens exactly one database file and rejects options that no longer mean anything
the pragma bootstrap is an ordered, once-only sequence whose effect is verified by read-back
every bound parameter is normalised before it reaches the binding
result columns are decoded from origin metadata, never from declared type names
64-bit integer values round-trip without precision loss
text that SQLite stores incorrectly is rejected at the boundary
no statement is issued with more bound parameters than the engine accepts
a long read does not starve the main thread
a result set is streamed across the worker boundary in batches, and a stream can never wedge the writer
a cancellable statement carries a per-row guard whose argument cannot be hoisted
statement deadlines are enforced in flight where a guard is possible, and detected at completion where it is not
every performance-dependent decision is blocked on measurements taken on a real filesystem under declared conditions
the decisions blocked on the measurement gate are named, and none of them is settled by this change
the conformance suite is re-executed against the new engine rather than amended to suit it
the event log is the only stored temporal representation and validity intervals are derived, never stored
gap-freedom is structural — a gap in a key's validity chain is unrepresentable
the structural gap-freedom guarantee is a property of the encoding, so converting a gap-bearing history into it is not information-preserving
getAt asserts the `at` bound through the primary-key index, not only through the index it searched
the event log is append-only at the database level
WellFormed is the single remaining refinement obligation and is asserted in the database
the write-timestamp clock policy is decided by the engine-core measurement gate, not assumed
same-transaction key reuse is adapter-enforced, and the adapter states exactly what it guarantees
the adapter never issues INSERT OR REPLACE against the event log
trigger assertions abort the statement and never end the transaction
the naive EXCLUDE transliteration is prohibited
the engine configuration under which trigger-based enforcement is sound is asserted, not assumed
Postgres errors surface as the shared StorageError hierarchy
Unconditional writes are gapless and monotonic (Law T1)
A caller-supplied transaction handle is honored or rejected, never silently ignored
put's CAS guard distinguishes conflict from absence
A second write to the same key within one transaction is rejected at the trigger level, not silently absorbed
listKeys streams without materializing the full result set first, and orders results correctly
getAt satisfies temporal-projection equivalence (Law T3), within the store's retention window
Dual addressing agrees at recorded write timestamps (Law T4)
History intervals never overlap for a single key (Law T5)

titles: per-key lease mutual exclusion is enforced in-process and uses no lock file
the lease's frozen observable contract is preserved under the new mechanism
a second writer process is detected and the displaced process is fail-stopped before it can commit
no UmbraDB code opens and closes a descriptor on the database file or its sidecars
every concurrency object in this capability is scoped per database file
the lease limitation stated in writing is exactly what the mechanism delivers
every write transaction opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE and no write path is DEFERRED
the whole-database write lock held by withTransaction is bounded
all lock waiting happens outside SQLite and busy_timeout is 0 on every handle
contention is retried inside the adapter and surfaces only through already-frozen codes
CONNECTION_ERROR becomes unreachable and is never repurposed
a transaction handle is poisoned by any transaction-scoped error, including one thrown before any statement reaches SQLite
read paths do not take the database write lock
prune's C2a justification is re-derived from BEGIN IMMEDIATE, not carried over
nested withTransaction resolves to a savepoint rather than deadlocking
P10 is re-executed with negative controls that fail against the implementations they target
Windows parity for the writer-generation guard is established before the strengthened contract ships
Migrations are idempotent and ordered
Schema isolation is the default, not opt-in
every object name UmbraDB creates carries the schema prefix, including index and trigger names
the schema parameter and DEFAULT_SCHEMA survive the engine change byte-for-byte
schema emulation SHALL NOT be implemented as one database file per schema
every table is STRICT and a wrong-typed write is rejected, not coerced
each PostgreSQL type class maps to exactly one SQLite declared type
domain constraints lost with the PostgreSQL type system are restored as named CHECK constraints
identifier containment is a junction table whose predicate is row-subset-of-the-finalizing-set
an identifier set is replaced wholesale on every write, never merged in place
uniqueness over a nullable key column is emulated by a coalesce expression index with a domain-excluded sentinel
listKeys matches a literal prefix with a half-open range scan, not LIKE
listKeys ordering is code-point order and the one-time resume-cursor reorder is disclosed
WITHOUT ROWID is used only for narrow tables and never for payload-bearing tables
migration 006 replays verbatim, and no future migration adds a STORED generated column to a populated table
the writer-generation table is created and seeded by the migration lineage
sequence allocation is guarded by a runtime invariant, with uniqueness as defence-in-depth
the schema text is covered by a digest recorded at migration time
every migration begins with non-idempotent DDL and runs in one transaction
transaction-history reads derive identifiers from entry and cross-check the junction
wallet-tier digest columns are declared under this capability's conventions
the forward-only migration framework is preserved with SQLite-native bootstrap detection
migration 005 is retained as a recorded no-op and its hard invariants are retired with reason
bulk inserts have no row cap derived from the bind-parameter ceiling
foreign-key enforcement is a schema precondition that is asserted, not assumed
every performance-dependent property is stated as an obligation to measure, not as a number
the durability probe verifies library-controlled pragmas instead of deployer-supplied server settings
the synchronous default is FULL and is lowered only under a stated decision rule
integrity coverage follows the three-class corruption model with an explicit column-level coverage set
the value digest is a versioned, length-prefixed, row-bound SHA-256 computed adapter-side
the digest covers the stored bytes and never a logical value
a documented-as-dangerous salvage bypass ships from day one
a covered row cannot be downgraded to unverified, by configuration or by statement
the schema digest is verified at open and is the one open-scoped corruption failure
the verification pass runs the structural check, the digest sweep, the schema digest and the invariants together, and never refuses
Class B corruption is answered by named invariants with an owner per change
the checksum VFS is considered and declined, with its reasons recorded
the integrity boundary is disclosed using the two-case wording, in every channel a consumer reads
corruption recovery is row-scoped and proportionate, never whole-database refusal
the cancellation contract promises only what a mechanism can deliver
the backup primitive is established by measurement on the ruled binding, not asserted
driver errors are discriminated by the ruled binding's string code, never by a numeric result code
a backup's manifest-to-chunk closure is tested rather than asserted
no frozen error code is repurposed and no contention code is added
every integrity fault raised by a sibling change is routed to a named existing code, and scope decides which
failures of a process outside the frozen surface are tool diagnostics, not catalog entries
the persisted value digest and the migration fidelity comparison are two distinct artifacts
CLOCK_REGRESSION retains its conditional retryability marking
the catalog count is derived from the exported surface and is not confused with the conformance pin
the stability policy binds the situation-to-code mapping and bounds additive-only
the release record prices every break as pre-tag and post-tag
the manual pre-tag evidence artifact is re-executed against the new release candidate, never amended
the conformance suite is re-executed with negative controls and gains the properties SQLite creates
deleting a pinned conformance id is a reviewed contract change in its own commit
a running embedded engine can be diagnosed from outside itself without a debugger
the unbounded transaction hold is documented as unbounded and instrumented rather than claimed to be bounded
every engine-named contract sentence is re-derived and every external precedent citation is re-verified before it ships
the known verification gaps are recorded in the catalog rather than left for a green gate to hide
the unmeasured integrity quantities are carried as obligations, never as assumptions

titles: the chain-archive lineage is created empty and replayed forward, with no data migration
the chain archive occupies its own database file and no transaction spans the tier boundary
a second process writing the archive file is detected and fail-stopped before it can commit
height-range separation SHALL NOT be implemented with ATTACH
each archive relation is stored in one table and a table-per-height-range layout is prohibited
a view-routing insert trigger never accepts a row it does not store
a height-qualified read resolves in one index descent
at most one canonical block per height is enforced by the database (invariant I-2)
the archive cursor is bounded by its data and its monotonic guard cannot latch
verifier-key observation identity uses the ruled coalesce expression index, not a plain UNIQUE
every PostgreSQL guard trigger has a named SQLite counterpart and row locking is removed with reason
blob content is stored in the database and verified on read by recomputing its address
the archive write path reuses prepared statements and acquires no bind-parameter row cap
the ingest cursor advances in the same transaction as the block bundle it passes
constraint identity survives the port and message parsing is confined to one function
the archive's bounded delete is written in the form that needs no optional compile option
a snapshot is a database file with no outstanding write-ahead-log dependency, together with a manifest
the snapshot and verification tooling runs outside the library process
the snapshot manifest is derived from the finished artifact, never from the source database
the snapshot manifest identifies the artifact well enough to restore it safely
restoring a snapshot runs four checks and reports them separately
a snapshot makes no completeness claim
no live-backup primitive is named for the archive until it has been measured on the ruled binding
the archive's durability setting is not lowered without four stated preconditions
each archive table has a stated integrity classification and mechanism
the digest column and its drift guard follow this lineage's DDL conventions
the uncovered projection tables have a written rebuild path with an executed transcript
the archive sync entry point remains coherent across typecheck, build and run
every performance-dependent property of the archive is an obligation to measure, not a number
the migration reads the source PostgreSQL database and never writes to it
the target database is created by running the SQLite lineage to completion on an empty file before any row is imported
the temporal event log is reconstructed from both source tables and the live version is never dropped
the reconstruction's source preconditions are verified per key rather than inherited from the adapter
a source state the event-log encoding cannot represent is refused, and no target database is produced
checkpoint manifest identifiers are preserved and no generated column is transported
the identifier array is exploded into the junction table and the two I-7 cross-checks hold on the imported data
a source that violates a constraint the target newly adds is refused with a remediation report, and is never quarantined
stored JSON values are transported as the source's own canonical text and never through a JavaScript JSON round trip
timestamps are transported as an exact millisecond integer under pinned session settings
objects belonging to the target lineage are produced by the lineage and are never imported
the export is a single read-only snapshot and the bundle is self-describing
verification is a ladder of five rungs whose pass is their conjunction, and it states what it assumes
point-in-time equivalence is established exhaustively over the breakpoint set
a check with nothing in scope reports n/a and never pass, and the fixtures are proven non-empty
migration-tool failures are tool diagnostics with a stable exit code and a machine-readable report
the stored-value digest and the transport-fidelity comparison are two distinct artifacts and are never conflated
content verification reuses the durability contract's digest regime and introduces no second mechanism
an interrupted migration never leaves a database that presents itself as complete
re-running the migration is safe, and resumability is decided by measurement rather than assumed
the import does not weaken any check in order to go faster
the supported rollback is the untouched source database and no reverse migration is offered
each distribution channel has a written procedure and the container channel's hazards are named
differences that survive a faithful migration are disclosed before the migration runs
no migration duration or throughput figure is asserted, and every PostgreSQL-side claim is labelled
